params.body:
Generations and lifestages as Trendwolves defines them in "Gentells Standard: Generaties & Lifestages" (Maarten Leyts, 5 October 2026). This replaces the 0.7.0 birth years, which followed Pew, and the empty lifestage ages.

## What changes

**Generations**

| | Born | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| Gen Z | 1995–2009 (was 1997–2012) | macro |
| ZAlpha | 2006–2012 (was 2008–2013) | micro: a lens over the border, never counted into Gen Z or Gen Alpha |
| Gen Alpha | 2010–2024 | macro |
| Gen Beta | 2025–2039 | macro, new status `reserved`: not tagged yet, the validator refuses it |

**Lifestages** now have ages and say what decides them:
- Kids 6–10.
- Tweens 9–10, a subgroup of Kids (`subgroupOf`).
- Teens 11–17, starting at the own smartphone and not at 13.
- Students 18–25.
- Young Adults 18–34.
- Young Families: parents of 25–39 whose youngest child is 0–10. It is now active.

Under 18 the device decides; from 18 the status decides, within the range. Children under 6 have no lifestage.

**Three modifier schemes from 18**, on signals and optional: `activities`, `households`, `relationships`.

**`rules/cohort.json`** holds the tagging rules:
- age is taken at the year of the signal;
- a generation comes from birth years, never from labels;
- a lifestage-only signal gets a generation only when its whole range falls inside one macro generation;
- tags freeze at observation;
- the lifestage birth years shift every 1 January.

`tools/rules.mjs` executes them: `generationsOf`, `lifestageBorn`, `lifestagesOf`, `generationOfLifestage`, `lifestageLabel`.

## Changed in practice

`rules/trend.json#cohort`: ZAlpha and Tweens no longer compete with the terms they lie over when a trend's cohort is chosen. Before, a ZAlpha signal that also carries Gen Z split the lead between them. A trend now carries a lens as well when more than half of its tagged signals carry it (`lensesOf`). The existing cohort cases give the same answers.

## Checks

- **New checks:** a gap or overlap between macro generations, a micro generation over no border, a subgroup outside its parent, and rule names that point nowhere.
- **Conformance:** the who-sits-where table for 2026–2030 from the document, generations from a birth year, lifestages from age and status, and the document's claims about the coming years. For example, 7 of 15 parent birth years are Gen Z in 2026 and 11 in 2030, and in 2030 all of ZAlpha is Students.
- **Ids stay:** `gen-alpha` keeps its id, and the document's `gen-genalpha` matches it as a hidden label.
- **Compatibility:** `npm test` passes 62 tests, and the release is compatible with v0.1.0 to v0.7.0.

## Open for Trendwolves

The document says a studying parent is Young Families, and also that the Young Families range starts at 25. This version keeps the range: a studying parent of 22 is Students. One line in the standard changes that if needed.

## After merge

A `v0.8.0` release, then the pipeline syncs to it and re-tags. That is a separate change.
params.title: 0.8.0 (proposed): generations and lifestages as Trendwolves defines them
